title: Migrate JS to TypeScript then add generic utility type — 3 turns
description: Plain JavaScript utility functions migrated to TypeScript with proper types, tests green, generic utility type added.

task_spec.prompt: Add proper TypeScript generics to `groupBy` in `src/utils.ts` — change signature to `groupBy<T>(arr: T[], keyFn: (item: T) => string | number): Record<string, T[]>`. Remove the `any` types. Run `npm test -- --forceExit`.
followup_prompts: Run `npm test -- --forceExit` to confirm no regressions. Now add generics to `pick<T extends object, K extends keyof T>(obj: T, keys: K[]): Pick<T, K>` and `omit<T extends object, K extends keyof T>(obj: T, keys: K[]): Omit<T, K>`. Walk me through what changed.

Final pass: implement `DeepPartial<T>` — a recursive type that makes all properties of T optional, including nested object properties. Use conditional type: `{ [K in keyof T]?: T[K] extends object ? DeepPartial<T[K]> : T[K] }`. Then run `npm test -- --forceExit` — all 5 tests must pass.
success_criteria: pick uses Pick<T, K> return type
omit uses Omit<T, K> return type
DeepPartial recursively makes all properties optional
